name: Sao Tome and Principe
sources: READ THIS FIRST. Sao Tome and Principe is the case the roster's iron rule about admitted gaps was written for. The World Bank's WDI carries EXACTLY ONE 1990 series for it - population. NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS and MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS all have no 1990 entry; the first WDI inflation print for the country is 1997 and the first external-debt print is 2001. So five of the eleven economic figures below come from the IMF or are brackets, and each says which it is. This file is the least well sourced in the roster and should be read that way.

GDP $0.12bn: IMF World Economic Outlook, NGDPD, STP, 1990 = 0.120 (billions of current US dollars). NOT the World Bank series the rest of this roster sits on, because that series has no 1990 print for Sao Tome. Cross-checked against the World Bank's own WITS country profile for STP 1990, which states GDP in current US dollars of 119 million - two World Bank and IMF surfaces agreeing on the same figure. Read alongside the vintage note in chad.json: for the five countries where both exist, IMF NGDPD runs 10-36% above the World Bank series, so this figure is probably a little high relative to its neighbours here rather than a little low.

Population 0.119m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series STP, 1990 = 119,211. The one properly sourced figure in this file, and the smallest population in the roster - a fifth of Bahrain's, a quarter of Equatorial Guinea's. The census of 4 August 1991 counted 117,504.

TFP trend -0.006: NOT SOURCED - there is no 1990 real growth print. Set level with the Central African Republic's -0.006 on the structure rather than on a number: Sao Tome was a cocoa monoculture whose roças had all been nationalised into fifteen state enterprises in 1975, whose Portuguese managers and technicians had left with them, and whose cocoa output had fallen from about 12,000 tonnes a year at independence to around 4,000 by the late 1980s. Cocoa was over 80% of export earnings and the world price in 1990 was the lowest in real terms in thirty years.

Inflation 42.2%: IMF World Economic Outlook, PCPIPCH, STP, 1990 = 42.2 (with 42.9% in 1989 and 46.5% in 1991, so the figure sits inside a consistent run rather than being a single odd print). FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG has no STP entry until 1997, which prints 35.8%. THIS IS THE ONE FIGURE IN THIS REGION THAT IS NOT A FRANC-ZONE NUMBER, and the contrast is the point of including the country: five BEAC members between -0.7% and 7.7%, and 250 km offshore a small-island economy with its own currency printing 42%. The dobra was not pegged to anything, the country imported essentially all of its food and all of its fuel, and Sao Tome joined the CFA franc's discipline only in 2010, by pegging to the euro.

Interest rate 36%: NOT SOURCED AND ENTERED AS A BRACKET. There is no published Banco Nacional de Sao Tome e Principe policy rate for 1990 that I could find, and the bank was a monobank doing central and commercial banking at once until it was split in 1992. 0.36 is set to put the real rate about six points below neutral, which is a fair description of a country under an IMF structural adjustment programme (SAP II ran 1990-1992) that was devaluing the dobra and rationing credit but not paying savers 42%. The loader's coupled check reads 0.025 - (0.36 - 0.422) = +0.087.

Revenue 15% of GDP: NOT SOURCED. A bracket, set above Equatorial Guinea's 12% and around Cameroon's sourced 14.26%. Sao Tome's tax base was the cocoa export levy and the customs house; the state's actual income was dominated by grants, which this field excludes by definition, and by 1990 aid inflows were of the same order as domestic revenue.

Military 0.8% of GDP: NOT SOURCED. The lowest figure in the roster, and it is entered low on composition rather than on a number: the Forcas Armadas de Sao Tome e Principe numbered about 600 men with no aircraft and two patrol boats. 0.8% of a $120m economy is about $1m a year, which is roughly what six hundred soldiers cost.

Investment 15% public and 5% private: NOT SOURCED - NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS has no STP entry for 1990. The 20% total is a bracket and it is high - just below Gabon's sourced 21.68% and above Congo's sourced 15.91%, in the poorest country in the region - and it is set there deliberately: capital formation in Sao Tome in this period was almost entirely donor-financed - the African Development Fund, the World Bank and Portugal rehabilitating plantations, the port at Ana Chaves and the road round Sao Tome island - which is why the split is weighted three to one to the public side. Both halves are judgements.

Debt 150% of GDP: NOT SOURCED AND THE WEAKEST FIGURE IN THIS FILE. DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS has no STP entry before 2001, which prints 423.55% of GNI - the highest debt ratio the World Bank has ever recorded for any country. Most of that accumulation is the 1990s: Sao Tome borrowed through the structural adjustment decade against a cocoa crop that kept failing. 1.5 is entered as a bracket for the start of that run: below Congo's sourced 2.12 and above Zaire's sourced 1.19, which is the right ordering for 1990 even though Sao Tome finished the decade worse than either. It is a judgement, and if this file is wrong anywhere it is probably here.

Oil 0.0 mbd: zero. The Gulf of Guinea Joint Development Zone with Nigeria was agreed in 2001 and has never produced commercially. In 1990 Sao Tome's fuel was all imported and paid for in dobras it did not have.

Stability 50 and authoritarianism 0.62: and this is the one hopeful file in the region. The Movimento de Libertacao de Sao Tome e Principe had been the sole legal party since independence on 12 July 1975 and Manuel Pinto da Costa president throughout, so on 1 January 1990 this is a one-party state and authoritarianism is entered above the model's ELECTORAL_CEILING of 0.60 accordingly - no elections at the start. But it is entered only just above, at 0.62, because the MLSTP had already decided to stop being one: the central committee resolved on multipartyism in December 1989, a new constitution went to referendum on 22 August 1990 and passed with 72%, and the country held the first free multi-party election in lusophone Africa on 20 January 1991 and then handed over power when it lost. Stability 50 is level with Ghana's and Cameroon's 52 and far above everything else in this region, and it is earned: no coup since 1975, no insurgency, no war, and a transition that worked. NOTHING HERE SCHEDULES THE REFERENDUM - the model is given a one-party state that is barely authoritarian and left to do what it does with it.

System Command: the fifteen state enterprises that the plantations became were still state-owned on 1 January 1990, prices and distribution were administered, and the constitutional revision that wrote in a market economy and private enterprise was the one that went to referendum in August 1990. Entered as Command for the same reason angola.json and tanzania.json are, and it is the field most likely to be wrong by the end of the first game year rather than at its start.

Separatism 0.12: Principe. The smaller island is 150 km from the larger, held about 6,000 of the country's 119,000 people, and its complaint - that everything was decided at Sao Tome and nothing was spent at Santo Antonio - was old and constant. It was answered rather than fought: Principe was given regional autonomy on 29 April 1995 with its own assembly and president. Entered at 0.12, above Gabon's 0.05 and below Equatorial Guinea's island-mainland 0.20, which is the right ordering - the same species of grievance, on a country with a tenth of the distance and none of the ethnic difference.

Military strength 0.1: about 600 men, no air force, two coastal patrol boats. THE LOWEST IN THE ROSTER. The only foreign force ever stationed on the islands was Angolan: roughly a thousand FAPLA troops sent by Luanda after the coup scare of 1978 and withdrawn in 1991, which is the relationship the relations file carries. A state with a hundred-strong navy and no enemy is a real object in this model and it should be priced as one.
